entry.title: 4th place at the European Cybersecurity & AI Hackathon Championship finals

link.title: 4th place at the European Cybersecurity & AI Hackathon Championship finals

entry.content:
After qualifying from the Vienna regional round in December, my teammates Tanja Šarčević, Yelyzaveta Klysa, Sabina Khazari, and I, team “4 braincells”, traveled to CISPA for the grand final of the European Cybersecurity & AI Hackathon Championship, joining 16 other regional winners from Paris, Vienna, Stockholm, Munich, Barcelona, and Warsaw.

We placed in the top 6 by score and advanced to the presentation round, which lifted us to 4th overall. The finals featured three challenges: localizing watermarked text regions, targeted attacks to misclassify training-set members, non-members, and generated images, and reconstructing face images from gradients.

Many thanks to Adam Dziedzic and Franziska Boenisch for organizing such a unique event, and to my teammates for a great run together. More details are available on the official CISPA Hackathon Championship page.
entry.summary: Our team placed 4th in the grand final of the CISPA European Cybersecurity & AI Hackathon Championship.

entry.title: Visiting the Dormant Neurons group at CISPA

link.title: Visiting the Dormant Neurons group at CISPA

entry.content:
At the turn of June and July, I visited the Dormant Neurons group at CISPA Helmholtz Center for Information Security for a short research exchange (June 30–July 1), hosted by Lea Schönherr. The group works on making AI systems more trustworthy, with a focus on generative and agentic systems.

Over two intense days we exchanged research interests and directions, and I gave a talk on rethinking long-standing assumptions in model stealing research. I am grateful to Lea and the group for the warm welcome and the many thoughtful discussions.
entry.summary: I visited the Dormant Neurons group at CISPA for a short research exchange.

entry.title: From Dagstuhl to a preprint on agentic AI in cybersecurity

link.title: From Dagstuhl to a preprint on agentic AI in cybersecurity

entry.content:
In April 2026 I attended my first Dagstuhl seminar, the Perspectives Workshop Autonomous AI Agents in Computer Security (26162), held at Schloss Dagstuhl on April 12–17.

Out of the discussions at the workshop grew a joint work, Rising From the Ashes: How Agentic AI is Unblocking Challenges in Cybersecurity, co-authored with Gabriela F. Ciocarlie, Kathrin Grosse, Somesh Jha, Andrew Paverd, and Christian Wressnegger, now available as a preprint on arXiv.

In the paper, we identify limitations that have rendered various cybersecurity approaches ineffective or inefficient, and map them to agentic AI capabilities that can help overcome these limitations.

Preprint: Rising From the Ashes: How Agentic AI is Unblocking Challenges in Cybersecurity.
entry.summary: A new preprint on agentic AI in cybersecurity, following my first Dagstuhl seminar.

entry.title: 2nd place at the Vienna round of the European Cybersecurity & AI Hackathon

link.title: 2nd place at the Vienna round of the European Cybersecurity & AI Hackathon

entry.content:
Last weekend I joined my colleagues Tanja Sarcevic, Yelyzaveta Klysa, and Sabina Khazari at the Trustworthy AI Hackathon in Vienna, organized by CISPA Helmholtz Center for Information Security.

Out of 16 teams, we finished 2nd and advanced to the championship grand final in St. Ingbert, Germany.

More details about the event are available on the official CISPA Hackathon Championship page.
entry.summary: We finished 2nd in Vienna and advanced to the CISPA championship grand final.

entry.title: Invited talk at ESSAI 2025
entry.content:
I was invited to speak at the European Symposium on Security and AI (ESSAI) in Rennes, France.

I presented our joint SaTML 2025 paper, Attackers Can Do Better: Over- and Understated Factors of Model Stealing Attacks, co-authored with Rudolf Mayer and Andreas Rauber.

Event details: ESSAI conference website.

Paper: IEEE Xplore.
entry.summary: I presented our SaTML paper at the European Symposium on Security and AI in Rennes.

entry.title: Winner of OCG Förderpreis 2025
entry.content:
I received the OCG Förderpreis 2025 from the Austrian Computer Society (OCG).

The award recognizes my master’s thesis, Man of Steal: Exploring Model Stealing Attacks Against Image Classifiers, completed at TU Wien under the supervision of Andreas Rauber and co-supervision of Rudolf Mayer.

Award details: OCG Förderpreis.
entry.summary: I received the OCG Förderpreis 2025 for my master’s thesis on model stealing attacks.
